title: LLM mods
summary: Every integration with LLM models is a mod: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Kilo Code, OpenRouter and LiteLLM come from the catalog of mods, and you can create your own on the site to connect another command-line program or an API compatible with OpenAI or Anthropic. Jev picks among all of them the same way, with the same gates, routing and usage records.
usage: Click Create mod in Settings › Mods (or Ctrl+K › Create mod): it opens Dashboard › Mods on the site, in the environment open in the app. For a command-line mod, give the program and its command line: {model} becomes the model Jev picked and {prompt}, alone in an argument, the request (without it, the request goes through standard input); if the program writes to the project, also give the planning line, which must not. For an API mod, choose OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic and enter the address. The mod reaches the app on the next sync: there, add the API key if it needs one (it stays on this computer), add or load its models and turn on the ones Jev may use. Edit the definition on the site or in the mod's tab. In an organization's projects its LLM policy applies to every mod: when it lists the allowed agents, the mods you create stay off there.
